reports.name: USDA Weekly Export Sales (delayed by Veterans Day)

outlook: Grains closed lower Thursday, with wheat leading the slide: December Minneapolis spring wheat fell 13 1/2 cents to $6.22, December Chicago wheat lost 15 1/4 cents and December corn dropped 5 1/2 cents to $4.42 1/2. January soybeans gave back 11 3/4 cents to $12.19 as the market struggled to hold its post-WASDE gains, with Brazil's soybean planting about two-thirds done and Conab's crop update due Friday; a stronger U.S. dollar also weighed on grains. Wheat stayed in its recent range after the Abu Dhabi Russia–Ukraine talks ended without a broad deal or reopening of Black Sea trade, while a drone strike on Russia's Ust-Luga port kept export risk in view. ICE January canola bucked the trend, up about C$6.80 to C$777.20 per tonne. Cash bids below are from Wednesday's Minneapolis report; Thursday's report comes out later.
